- Question a, level: Too easy for Year 12 VCE. The distractors are plainly illogical (e.g. 'Low skills make people feel able'), so a student can pick the answer without understanding the skill–participation relationship.

rejected.title: Skills, participation and performance
card: A motor skill is a movement that is learned and controlled to reach a goal, such as catching a ball or swimming freestyle.
People who have the skills for an activity often feel more able to do it. They are more likely to join in and to keep playing.
Taking part gives more practice. More practice can improve skills further, which can lift performance.
The link works in both directions. Skills can support participation, and participation can build skills. Without skills, people may drop out or avoid the activity.
rejected.remember: Skills can raise participation, and participation gives practice that can raise skills and performance.

a.q: Which statement best explains how developing motor skills can increase participation?
opts: Skills make people feel able, so they tend to join in
Skills end the need for practice, so people tend to join in
Taking part makes skills less needed, so people keep playing
Low skills make people feel able, so they tend to join in
a.why: Having the skills for an activity can make a person feel more able to do it, so they are more likely to take part and keep going. Skills do not end the need for practice, because taking part gives practice that can build skills further. People with low skills are more likely to drop out, not join in.
a.clue: Practice keeps helping even after skills develop.

b.q: Aisha, 13, struggled to kick a football, so she stopped joining lunchtime games. Her teacher runs weekly kicking sessions and she attends. Which outcome is the most likely over time?
opts: Her skills improve, so she joins in and gets more practice
Her skills stay the same, but she joins games for fun
Her skills improve, but she has no reason to join games
Her skills improve only if she avoids games and trains alone
b.why: The sessions give practice, so her kicking is likely to improve. Better skills can make Aisha feel more able, so she is more likely to join games, which give more practice. Joining games for fun without better skills ignores why she stopped: low skill led her to avoid them.
b.clue: What did low skill lead her to do at first?

b.clue: Follow the link from skill to taking part, then back to practice.
